newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady, overnight seen down.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady, overnight seen down.

text.p: Interbank rates in Kuala Lumpur were mostly unchanged as the market remained liquid, but the overnight rate was expected to come down due to a maturity, dealers said on Friday.
They said a mismatch in funds flow after the payment of one billion ringgit for two Bank Negara bill issues on Wednesday was neutralised by the maturity of a 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill.
"The overnight should come down substantially," said the head of money dealing at a foreign bank.
He said the market was otherwise a bit cautious, wondering why interest rates were not falling despite a sharp rise in liquidity on the back of a strengthening ringgit.
The ringgit has gained around two percent against the U.S. dollar in the last 10 days.
One-week money was at 7.10/20 percent, two-week at 7.10/20, one- and three-month at 7.25 and six-month at 7.35/38, all unchanged from their previous levels.
Dealers said the market is expected to remain flush next week and bring down interbank rates further.
